chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:
about a man who performs ẓihār against his bondwoman, so he said: “The free woman and the bondwoman are equal in this matter.”

key_terms.سَوَاءٌ: equal; the same in legal ruling here
key_terms.يُظَاهِرُ: to perform ẓihār, declaring a woman unlawful by likening her to one permanently forbidden

ai.seo_question: Does the ruling of ẓihār apply equally to a free woman and a bondwoman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ẓihār and states that the ruling applies equally whether the woman is free or a bondwoman. It shows that in this specific juristic matter, the legal status does not differ between the two.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4848 - Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as))

about a man who performs ẓihar (a form of divorce by comparison) against his female slave.
Imam (as) replied: "In this matter, a free woman and a bondwoman are the same."
